title: Mastering ECLAT: Support-Based Approach to Market Basket Optimization

cues.en: -: Hello and welcome back to the course on Machine Learning.
cues.zh: 講師：大家好，歡迎回到機器學習課程。

cues.en: Today we're continuing exploring association rule learning and we're talking about the intuition behind the ACLA model.
cues.zh: 今天繼續探索關聯規則學習，談 Eclat 模型背後的直覺概念。

cues.en: So the ACLA model is very, very simple.
cues.zh: Eclat 模型非常簡單。

cues.en: After we have already studied the A Priori model, it's kind of like a simplified version.
cues.zh: 學過 Apriori 模型後，它有點像簡化版。

cues.en: Alright, so let's have a look.
cues.zh: 來看看。

cues.en: It also talks about, the ACLA model also talks about "people who bought, also bought".
cues.zh: Eclat 模型一樣在談「買了這個的人，也買那個」。

cues.en: So it's kind of like a recommender system.
cues.zh: 有點像推薦系統。

cues.en: And similar to what we had in the A Priori algorithm, here we've got for instance, movies and we've got some potential rules.
cues.zh: 和 Apriori 演算法類似，這裡例如有電影，以及一些潛在規則。

cues.en: So basically exactly the same things, if you've got your movie list or movies that people liked, people who like movie one,
cues.zh: 基本上完全相同。如果有電影清單，或大家喜歡的電影，喜歡電影一的人，

cues.en: or just generally looks like if somebody likes movie one, they're very likely to like movie two.
cues.zh: 整體看來很可能也喜歡電影二。

cues.en: If they like movie two, they're likely to like movie four.
cues.zh: 喜歡電影二，可能也喜歡電影四。

cues.en: If they like movie one, they might like movie three.
cues.zh: 喜歡電影一，可能喜歡電影三。

cues.en: Again, these rules have, will have different strength, but here we aren't actually going to be talking about rules per se because the ACLA model is different
cues.zh: 一樣，這些規則強度不同，但這裡其實不會嚴格談規則本身，因為 Eclat 模型不同於

cues.en: to the A Priori model.
cues.zh: Apriori 模型。

cues.en: In the A Priori model, we came up with rules towards the end, that's the output and we, based on the lift, we could judge the strength of each rule.
cues.zh: Apriori 最後會產生規則作為輸出，並透過提升度判斷每條規則的強度。

cues.en: Whereas here we are going to be talking about sets and you'll see why just now.
cues.zh: 這裡則要談集合，等一下就知道為什麼。

cues.en: So here we've got the market basket as optimization.
cues.zh: 這是購物籃最佳化。

cues.en: Same thing that people who buy burgers are likely to buy french fries as well.
cues.zh: 一樣，買漢堡的人也可能買薯條。

cues.en: People who buy vegetables are likely to buy fruits, and these are just some potential rules.
cues.zh: 買蔬菜的人可能買水果，這只是一些潛在規則。

cues.en: So we're not saying they're strong or some potential outcomes that we're looking at.
cues.zh: 不是說它們很強，只是可能觀察的結果。

cues.en: We're not saying that they're strong or we're not selecting and we're just saying what could potentially be.
cues.zh: 不是說很強，也還沒選，只是在說可能的情況。

cues.en: And then the ACLA model is the responsible for actually going through all of these combinations and telling us what we should focus on.
cues.zh: Eclat 模型負責走遍這些組合，告訴我們該著重哪些。

cues.en: Alright, so in the ACLA model, just like in the A Priori model, we have the support factor.
cues.zh: 和 Apriori 一樣，Eclat 也有支持度這個因素。

cues.en: So previously in the A Priori model we had, or the algorithm we had support, we had confidence, and we had lift.
cues.zh: 先前 Apriori 模型或演算法中，有支持度、信賴度與提升度。

cues.en: In the ACLA model, we only have support.
cues.zh: Eclat 只有支持度。

cues.en: So we only are looking at, okay, so people who are watching a certain combinations of movies,
cues.zh: 只看某種電影組合，

cues.en: how often does this happen?
cues.zh: 出現得有多頻繁。

cues.en: And here, just bear in mind that M doesn't mean just one movie.
cues.zh: 要記得，這裡 M 不只代表一部電影。

cues.en: And this was the same for A Priori.
cues.zh: Apriori 其實也是一樣。

cues.en: It was just easier for us to understand the intuition based on one movie or one product.
cues.zh: 只是用一部電影或一項產品，比較容易理解概念。

cues.en: But actually M and I, what they stand for is a set of items or a set of movies.
cues.zh: 實際上 M 和 I 代表電影集合或項目集合。

cues.en: So as specifically in the ACLA model, it doesn't really make sense to look at, you know, an item by itself because we don't have the confidence
cues.zh: 尤其在 Eclat 中，單看一項產品不太有意義，因為沒有信賴度

cues.en: and the lift factors.
cues.zh: 與提升度這兩個因素。

cues.en: We're only looking at support.
cues.zh: 只看支持度。

cues.en: So we're just looking at how frequently does this set of items occur.
cues.zh: 只看這個項目集合出現得多頻繁。

cues.en: So if we're just gonna look at a set of items which contains only one item, then we're just looking at the frequency at how, what is the popularity of movies?
cues.zh: 如果只看包含單一項目的集合，就只是在看頻率，也就是電影的熱門程度。

cues.en: And that is very trivial.
cues.zh: 這很簡單。

cues.en: So we're not going to be looking at that.
cues.zh: 所以不看這種情況。

cues.en: We're going to be aiming for at least two items in a set.
cues.zh: 目標是每個集合至少兩個項目。

cues.en: And therefore M here stands for a set of two movies or more.
cues.zh: 因此，這裡 M 代表兩部或更多電影的集合。

cues.en: And what we're calculating for a support, we're calculating, okay, what is, how often does this set of two movies,
cues.zh: 計算支持度，就是算這個兩部電影的集合，

cues.en: let's say, Interstellar and X Machine, how often does it occur in all of the watch lists?
cues.zh: 例如《星際效應》和《人造意識》，在所有觀影清單中出現多少次。

cues.en: Or what percentage of watch lists, or what percentage of lists of movies that people liked, contain those two together?
cues.zh: 或者多少比例的觀影清單、喜愛電影清單，同時包含兩部。

cues.en: Not just one of them, but those two together.
cues.zh: 不只是其中一部，而是兩部都有。

cues.en: And let's say, hypothetically, if 100% of the lists that you had in a large data set contain
cues.zh: 假設大型資料集裡，100% 的清單都同時包含

cues.en: both movies together then that would imply that, you know, anybody who likes Interstellar likes X Machine, anyone who likes X Machine likes Interstellar,
cues.zh: 這兩部，就表示喜歡《星際效應》的人都喜歡《人造意識》，喜歡《人造意識》的人也都喜歡《星際效應》，

cues.en: and pretty much so if anybody has seen even one of those movies that you need to recommend that movie, the other one to them.
cues.zh: 所以只要有人看過其中一部，就應該向他推薦另一部。

cues.en: Or if you had like 80% of your lists had those two movies together that basically means there's a high likelihood that they come in pairs, right?
cues.zh: 如果 80% 的清單同時有這兩部，基本上表示它們很可能成對出現，對吧？

cues.en: That if somebody liked one of them then they'll like that one.
cues.zh: 喜歡其中一部，就會喜歡另一部。

cues.en: Same thing for transactions.
cues.zh: 交易也是一樣。

cues.en: Like if you have chips and burgers and, you know, 75% of all of your orders, right?
cues.zh: 例如所有訂單中，75% 都有薯條和漢堡。

cues.en: Then if somebody's just buying burgers, then they'll likely to, then when you recommend chips to them, there's a 75% chance that they will also be interested
cues.zh: 如果有人只買漢堡，你推薦薯條，就有 75% 的機會他也感興趣，

cues.en: or will like to buy chips with their burgers.
cues.zh: 或想把薯條和漢堡一起買。

cues.en: And it's a very, very trivial approach.
cues.zh: 這是非常簡單的方法。

cues.en: And that's pretty much it.
cues.zh: 大致就是這樣。

cues.en: That's all there is to the ACLA model.
cues.zh: Eclat 模型的內容就這些。

cues.en: It's much faster, and the steps involved are set a minimum support, so you want to set your support level at which you want to only
cues.zh: 它快得多，步驟是先設定最低支持度，也就是一個

cues.en: below which you want to disregard anything, then you take all the subsets in transactions having higher support then the min support and then you sort the subset in decreasing support.
cues.zh: 低於它就忽略的下限，再取交易中支持度高於下限的所有子集，依支持度遞減排序。

cues.en: And basically at the top you will have the strongest combinations of items, which you should look at.
cues.zh: 最上方就是最強的項目組合，應該優先看。

cues.en: Maybe, you know, you'll look at the top 10 or top file or something like that.
cues.zh: 例如看前十、前五名之類的。

cues.en: So that's pretty much it.
cues.zh: 大致如此。

cues.en: That's all the ACLA model is.
cues.zh: 這就是 Eclat 模型。

cues.en: And as you can see, it's much easier to understand after you already know a bit about the A Priori.
cues.zh: 可以看到，了解一點 Apriori 之後，就容易理解得多。

cues.en: Alright, hope you enjoyed this tutorial, and off we go to Hadlan to implement this in practice.
cues.zh: 希望你喜歡這堂，接下來交給 Hadelin 實作。

cues.en: And I'll see you here next time.
cues.zh: 我們下次在這裡見。

cues.en: Until then, happy analyzing.
cues.zh: 在那之前，祝你分析愉快。
